neighbours.label: final word of a stock multiword connective phrase (be that as it may, in the wake of, on the off chance, notwithstanding)
fire: The hotel is old and the rooms are small. Be that as it may, the staff are lovely.
Prices rose sharply. Be that as it may, sales kept climbing all year.
Bring a coat on the off chance that the weather turns cold.
In the wake of the scandal, the director resigned.
The road is narrow; be that as it may, trucks use it daily.
Keep some cash on hand on the off chance that the card fails.
The town rebuilt quickly in the wake of the earthquake.
The plan is costly. Be that as it may, it is our best option.
quiet: The hotel is old and the rooms are small. Even so, the staff are lovely.
Prices rose sharply. Still, sales kept climbing all year.
Bring a coat in case the weather turns cold.
After the scandal, the director resigned.
The road is narrow; even so, trucks use it daily.
Keep some cash on hand in case the card fails.
The town rebuilt quickly after the earthquake.
The plan is costly. Still, it is our best option.

notes: card top: off chance, In the wake, Not|withstanding, Be that as it may, a large number, mostly in spun SEO prose; + pole is plain connectives (However, Additionally, due). Probe: only 'Be that as it may' fired (0.38); off chance, wake, notwithstanding, large number near zero in clean prose. Weak guess.
